ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the square ABCD, points E and F are located on BC and CD, respectively. AE intersects BF at point G, and AC intersects BF at point H. If CE = DF, BG = GH, and AB = 2, what is the area of $\triangle CFH$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $FM\perp CH$ at point $M$. \\
$\because$ Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=\angle BCD=\angle BAD=90^\circ$, $AB=BC=2$, $\angle BAC=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAD$, $\angle ACD=\frac{1}{2}\angle BCD$.\\
$\therefore AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}+2^{2}}=2\sqrt{2}$, $\angle BAC=45^\circ$, $\angle ACD=45^\circ$.\\
Moreover, $\because CE=DF$,\\
$\therefore BC-CE=CD-DF$.\\
$\therefore BE=CF$.\\
In $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle BCF$,\\
$\begin{cases} AB=BC, \\ \angle ABE=\angle BCF, \\ BE=CF. \end{cases}$\\
$\therefore \triangle ABE\cong \triangle BCF$ (SAS).\\
$\therefore \angle 1=\angle 2$.\\
Moreover, $\because \angle ABE=\angle ABG+\angle 2=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABG+\angle 1=90^\circ$.\\
$\therefore \angle AGB=180^\circ-(\angle ABG+\angle 1)=90^\circ$.\\
Moreover, $\because BG=GH$,\\
$\therefore AH=AB=2$.\\
$\therefore CH=AC-AH=2\sqrt{2}-2$.\\
In $\triangle ABG$ and $\triangle AHG$,\\
$\begin{cases} AB=AH, \\ AG=AG, \\ BG=HG. \end{cases}$\\
$\therefore \triangle ABG\cong \triangle AHG$ (SSS).\\
$\therefore \angle 1=\angle HAG$.\\
$\therefore \angle BAC=\angle 1+\angle HAG=2\angle 1=45^\circ$.\\
$\therefore \angle 1=22.5^\circ$.\\
$\therefore \angle 2=\angle 1=22.5^\circ$.\\
$\therefore \angle BFC=180^\circ-\angle 2-\angle BCF=180^\circ-22.5^\circ-90^\circ=67.5^\circ$.\\
$\therefore \angle CHF=180^\circ-\angle HCF-\angle HFC=180^\circ-45^\circ-67.5^\circ=67.5^\circ$.\\
$\therefore \angle CHF=\angle CFH$.\\
$\therefore CH=CF=2\sqrt{2}-2$.\\
$\because MF\perp HC$, $\angle ACD=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle MFC=180^\circ-\angle FMC-\angle MCF=45^\circ$\\
$\therefore FM=MC$.\\
In $\triangle FMC$, $FC^{2}=MC^{2}+MF^{2}$.\\
$\therefore {(2\sqrt{2}-2)}^{2}=2MF^{2}$.\\
$\therefore MF=2-\sqrt{2}$.\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle FHC}=\frac{1}{2}MF\cdot HC=\frac{1}{2}(2\sqrt{2}-2)(\sqrt{2}-2)=\boxed{3\sqrt{2}-4}$.

Since in the figure B, G, H, F are collinear and the order is B-G-H-F, and BG=GH, on the same straight line distance is proportional to the difference in x-coordinates, so x_H=2x_G. Thus 4/(t+2)=8t/(t^2+4). Solving gives t^2+4t-4=0, taking the positive root t=2√2-2.

Thus x_H=4/(t+2)=√2. Triangle CFH takes CF as the vertical base, CF=t=2√2-2; the horizontal distance from point H to line CD, namely x=2, is 2-x_H=2-√2. Therefore the area is S=1/2·CF·(2-x_H)=1/2(2√2-2)(2-√2)=3√2-4.
